anomalies.observed: The netlist places a 2-pin screw terminal J5 on the heater-control net: J5 pin 2 is connected to /Microcontroller/HEATER, and J5 pin 1 is connected to GND. This makes the ESP32 GPIO1 / U6 IN+DIAG_EN node available on a field screw terminal.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes a single heater output path driven by U6 and brought out to J6, and does not describe any field screw terminal on the 3.3 V GPIO1 heater-control net. A screw terminal connected to a GPIO output and GND is an unintended external short/interference path unless explicitly specified.

evidence.quote: Drives a single heater output net through a smart high-side switch (U6, TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1) switched from the ESP32's GPIO1

anomalies.impact: If the J5 terminal is wired or jumpered, GPIO1 / U6 IN+DIAG_EN can be pulled to ground, preventing the heater from turning on and potentially overloading the ESP32 output driver. If an external voltage is applied to J5, it can stress the MCU GPIO and the U6 input.

parsed.summary: Most of the netlist matches the specification, but an undocumented screw terminal J5 is connected between the heater-control GPIO net and GND, creating an unintended external short/interference path not described in the intended design.
